Name: Pre-Pesach Foraging - 21 April 2024
Description:
with Michael Green

(Intrepid Forager & London National Park City Ranger)

Join us on the Heath, where we will learn how to identify 10-15 common edible wild plants, including maror - bitter herbs - for the Seder plate.

Have you ever wondered how to tell tasty plants apart from their poisonous cousins? Or wanted to connect with nature and the seasons in a deeper way? Edible plants are all around us in the city, so join us for a guided foraging walk and get to know your botanical neighbours.

Jews, too, have a tradition of foraging and wild food is an inspiring way to connect with our roots as a people. We will learn how to identify 10-15 common edible wild plants, including maror - bitter herbs - for the Seder plate, plus how to prepare and enjoy them at home.

From wild salads and soups, to herbal teas and pickles - there's a whole world of wild food waiting to be discovered.

The walk will be led by London National Park City Ranger, Michael Green (www.instagram.com/londonfungusnetwork) and last around 2.5-3 hours, including foraged herbal tea. All you need to bring is yourselves, a pen, notepad - and a resuable cup!

Name: Veganuary Cooking Class
Description:
Vegan Cooking Class: Discover Delicious, Nutritious Plant-Based Dishes Join our experienced resident chef and community engagement manager, Zoe, as she teaches you how to create delicious plant-based dishes inspired by global cuisines. Zoe will guide you through essential vegan cooking techniques, including how to build umami-rich flavors and create hearty, "meaty" dishes using plant-based ingredients. By the end of the class, you'll have learned valuable skills, enjoyed a delicious vegan feast, and taken home the recipes to recreate the meals at home. What to Expect:
  • A fun, interactive 3-hour cooking experience
  • Step-by-step guidance on preparing a variety of vegan dishes
  • Tips on maximizing flavor and creating balanced, nutritious meals
  • A satisfying, delicious lunch shared with the group
  • Recipes emailed to you after the class 
  • Refreshments and a warm, welcoming atmosphere
Feel free to arrive up to 30 minutes before the class to enjoy a cup of tea and meet fellow participants. The class begins at 11:30am, and we’ll sit down to enjoy the meal together around 2:15pm. Don’t forget to bring an apron and a container in case there are any delicious leftovers to take home!

Name: Gujarati Feast - A Taste of North India: 24th January 2025
Short description: Gujarati Friday Night Feast: A Taste of North India Join us for our first Friday night dinner of 2025 and get inspired for Veganuary! Start the year with a delicious, plant-based journey through the heart of India! Chef Nishma of Shambhu’s will be preparing an exclusive Indian feast, showcasing her expertise in North Indian and Gujarati cuisine. Nishma, who is from a Jain Indian background and grew up in Kenya, has been running her exclusively vegan catering business, Shambhu's for nearly 20 years. For this special dinner, she will be preparing a fantastic spread of North Indian dishes – a cuisine she knows and loves deeply. Expect a feast of hearty and flavorful dishes, including roasted aubergine curry, toor dal, fresh rotis, and a traditional Indian dessert.

Name: Six Inches of Soil Screening and Q and A
Description:
To mark Tu B'Shevat (New Year of the trees) we are screening Six Inches of Soil film. The film tells the story of remarkable farmers, communities, small businesses, chefs and entrepreneurs who are leading the way to transform how our food is produced and consumed.

As part of the evening there will be a vegan stew made from locally sourced and organic vegetables.

The screening will be followed by a Q and A with Dr Lucy Michaels, researcher and impact producer for the film and Wendy Alcock a community gardener from Incredible Edible Barnet.

Arrive between 6 and 6.25pm for mingling and a bowl of stew. Screening will start at 6.30pm followed by a Q and A and more mingling. The event will finish by around 9/9.30pm

The £10 per head is to cover our costs, including the licensing fee. Any profit made on top of this will go directly to the six inches of soil non-profit organisation.

Description:

We will be sowing and learning about seed to germination process and growing seedlings. We ask that those who join to take home their seed pots, to grow on a sunny window sill at home and to bring back in around 4 to 6 weeks at our first outdoor gardening session of 2025. Practical instructions and equipment will be given on the day. Whilst we will provide the seeds, if you have any spare seeds at home, feel free to also bring these.

We will come up with a joint vision for the JVS garden and hear about how you would like to get involved.

As part of this ongoing series of sessions, we are looking for volunteers to get involved in the garden and to develop it into a food growing space. Whatever time you have, small or big, we would love you to get involved.

Name: Blessed hands
Short description:
Blessed Hands // Bendichas Manos
Cooking Up a Show With My Turkish Jewish Granny

Find yourself transported to late Ottoman Turkey, to Spain of 1492, to an unnamed Middle Eastern city. Cook a delectable meal inspired by these places and others in the SWANA (South West Asia and North Africa) region, all while asking, what is authentic in this food? What makes anything authentic? And Why!?

Join anthropologist and performer Dr. Michal Nahman for a unique cookery masterclass and theatrical performance blending song, dance, and comedy.

Leading us through a menu based on several years of interviews with her Sephardi Jewish family, as well as her many collaborators from Jewish, Muslim, Christian and British backgrounds researching food diasporas in the UK.
This debut show launches the Arts and Humanities Research Council funded production of Blessed Hands/Bendichas Manos. We'll finish by sharing the meal we've cooked together.

Early bird ticket up until 30th June: £30. After this tickets will be £35. Spaces are limited and we anticipate this event will sell out, so early booking recommended.
